record.original_question: Consider a foliation F defined by a fibration with closed basis B and fiber F and π1 (F ) = Zk . Under what hypothesis does any foliation G close to F have a compact leaf close to a fiber?

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. Consider a foliation F defined by a fibration with closed basis B and fiber F and π1 (F ) = Zk . Under what hypothesis does any foliation G close to F have a compact leaf close to a fiber?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold equipped with a smooth foliation $\mathcal{F}$ whose leaves are the fibers of a smooth fibration $\pi : M \to B$ with closed base $B$ and typical fiber $F$. Assume that $\pi_1(F) \cong \mathbb{Z}^k$ for some integer $k \geq 1$. Say that a smooth foliation $\mathcal{G}$ on $M$ (of the same dimension as $\mathcal{F}$) is "close to $\mathcal{F}$" if its tangent distribution is $C^r$-close (for some fixed $r \geq 1$) to that of $\mathcal{F}$, and that a compact leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{G}$ is "close to a fiber" of $\pi$ if $L$ is $C^r$-close (as an embedded submanifold) to some fiber $\pi^{-1}(b)$.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient hypotheses on the triple $(M, \pi, F)$ — for instance, conditions on the holonomy of $\mathcal{F}$, on the topology of $B$ and $F$, or on the action of $\pi_1(B)$ on $\pi_1(F) \cong \mathbb{Z}^k$ — under which the following persistence property holds: every smooth foliation $\mathcal{G}$ on $M$ sufficiently close to $\mathcal{F}$ admits at least one compact leaf close to a fiber of $\pi$.
artifact.category_tag: Foliations and persistence of compact leaves
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about identifying hypotheses that guarantee persistence of a compact leaf (close to a fiber) under perturbation of a foliation defined by a fibration with fiber having free abelian fundamental group. Classical results (Reeb stability, Langevin–Rosenberg type theorems, and recent work on persistence of compact leaves) address related but more restrictive settings, and no general answer for $\pi_1(F) \cong \mathbb{Z}^k$ appears to be established in the surveyed literature.

status_evidence.title: Periodic leaves for diffeomorphisms preserving codimension-one foliations
status_evidence.snippet: A foliation has the compact leaf persistence property if every foliation C^r close to it has at least a compact leaf.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of compact leaf persistence is an established but partial framework in foliation theory.

status_evidence.title: Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Calegari)
status_evidence.snippet: Stability results à la Reeb: in a neighborhood of a compact leaf with finite holonomy, nearby foliations have nearby compact leaves.
status_evidence.claim: Existing stability results assume strong hypotheses (e.g. finite holonomy) on the compact leaf, leaving the case of $\pi_1(F)=\mathbb{Z}^k$ generally unresolved.
